protocol.title: PE beads · Exp 04 · PSF, plane response and axial scaling
protocol.summary: Measure the point response, the thin-sheet (plane) response H(z) and the dry-to-water focal scaling for each objective and pinhole.

children.body: The integrated bead signal depends on H(z), the response to a thin fluorescent sheet.

attrs.title: PSF, plane response and axial scaling

children.body: Pins: lateral and on-axis axial FWHM against pinhole (4a); the plane response H(z) and its shape (4b); the focal scaling factor from stage travel to depth in water (4c).

Model (simulator): 20x/0.75 at 1 AU gives 0.40 µm lateral, 1.5 µm on-axis and 2.6 µm plane-integrated axial FWHM; 10x at 4 AU gives a 28 µm plane response with a flat top. The textbook formula for the 20x at 1 AU gives 2.3 µm (n = 1).

rows.free_text: 100–200 nm orange/red fluorescent beads, diluted 1:1000 in water (4a)
PE-detection antibody at ≈10 nM, no beads (4d)
PE-detection antibody in PBS, 200 µL per well (4b)
Chamber of known height: a calibrated spacer (50–120 µm, measured with a micrometer) between two #1.5 coverslips, sub-resolution beads stuck to both inner surfaces, filled with water (4c)

children.body: Acquisition grid

Before any quantitative acquisition: stand and lasers on for 2–3 h; 561 nm excitation; the same PE emission band (e.g. 570–620 nm) every time; 16-bit with fine integration (the default is 12-bit, so check the file); one HV and one offset for the whole session; background mode at least 50 DN above zero; no saturated pixels. Record the transmitted-light channel with every PE frame: beads are found in it, never in PE. Find focus in transmitted light and hold it with Perfect Focus. Never live-scan PE to focus.

outputs.name: sect_um
outputs.label: Textbook optical section (PH ≥ 1 AU)
outputs.expr: sqrt((0.88 * lam_em / (n_imm - sqrt(n_imm ^ 2 - na ^ 2))) ^ 2 + (sqrt(2) * n_imm * ph_um / na) ^ 2)

outputs.name: equator_nominal
outputs.label: Stage travel from glass to bead equator

children.body: At NA [!var:na] and [!var:ph_au]: the pinhole is [!var:ph_um] at the sample and the textbook section is [!var:sect_um]. The bead equator sits [!var:equator_nominal] of stage travel above the glass.
Point response
Dry 10 µL of the diluted sub-resolution beads on the glass, then cover with water.
For each objective and pinhole in the grid, z-stack ≥10 isolated beads at low power (1 µW at 20x, 3 µW at 10x).
Plane response H(z)
Add 200 µL of PE-antibody at 1 µg/mL to an empty glass-bottom well, wait 30 min at room temperature, wash 3× with PBS, leave PBS on.
Find the layer at very low power. Then for each objective and pinhole, z-scan through it to ±20 µm (the tails matter) at the steps in the grid. Use a fresh spot for every scan (the layer bleaches).
Glass-to-solution edge (axial weight and T)

Fill a well with PE-antibody at ≈10 nM (no beads). z-scan from 10 µm below the glass surface to 30 µm into the solution, 0.25 µm steps, for each objective at 1 AU and the largest AU NIS allows. Read the largest AU per objective from NIS and record it.
Axial scaling

In the chamber of known height, at 20x and 1 AU, z-stack from below the bottom bead layer to above the top one, 0.2 µm steps. Do not use the assay beads for this: a polystyrene bead refracts like a weak lens and shifts its own top peak.
4a: fit Gaussians to the lateral and axial profiles of each bead; report median FWHM against pinhole.
4b: mean intensity of the central field against z is H(z). Report its FWHM and its shape: flat-topped, Gaussian, or with 1/z² tails. Send the H(z) table, because the simulator can use it directly.
4c: z_scale = (true chamber height) / (nominal stage travel between the two bead layers). Expect ≈1.33 for a dry objective into water.

4d: the solution signal rises across the glass edge; its derivative against z is the axial weight w(z). Its integral is ℓ_eff, and T = (∫ of w from −4 to +4 µm) / ℓ_eff is the fraction of the section that falls inside a bead. Expected T ≈ 0.84–0.95 at 20x/0.80, 1 AU.
Decision: whether the 10x open-pinhole H(z) is flat across ±4 µm (the focus tolerance of the high-throughput mode), and the Perfect Focus offset to the bead equator.
Record for every acquisition

children.body: Save the .nd2 files as acquired (no 8-bit export, no LUT) in a folder outside the website repo, e.g. BeadConfocalData/<date>_<exp>/, and fill one plate-map CSV row per well or field (columns are listed in Research/PE_bead_confocal_experiments.md, section 7).
